01.reason: A real incident (pledge written, ketubah lost, denial, witnesses, claim of payment) brought before R. Hiyya, but it is mostly claims and counterclaims resolved by a ruling, a courtroom case with little narrated change.

02.reason: A habitual practice of Abaye's mother followed by the Gemara's objection; a custom that leads nowhere.

03.reason: A lexical dispute illustrated by a one-line report of a man hawking willow; a bare report cited as evidence with no story development.

04.reason: Exegetical opinions followed by a meeting with Elijah that only frames a question and answer; setting plus Q&A without conflict is not a story.

05.reason: An illustrative case of two rabbis each swearing about Rav's teaching; speech acts in ordinary scholarly disagreement, cited to define a legal category.

06.reason: A local custom reported to Rav Yosef, who orders a demonstration, followed by legal debate; the outcome is only implied and nothing further is narrated.

07.reason: Reish Lakish's legal argument addressed to the Elders of the South; pure speech in scholarly debate.

08.reason: The narrative of Hananiah son of Azzur's false prophecy and death is a biblical episode retold; the following segment is legal discussion about it.

09.reason: Shmuel veers off the road and Rav Yehuda questions him; one real action followed by a question and answer, mainly speech.

10.reason: Forbidden fat falls into a pot and Rav Asi considers how to measure, then the Rabbis challenge him; one event followed by legal discussion with nothing changing.

11.reason: A description of a recurring Temple practice and Rava's personal custom embedded in legal-exegetical discussion; no one-time event.

12.reason: A sale, the buyer's distress and the seller's reassuring promise form a small incident, but what follows is only legal discussion of the promise's validity.

13.reason: The vote in the upper story of Nitza's house only frames a halakhic ruling; no narrated event beyond the decision.

14.reason: A bereavement and Rabba bar bar Hana's intentions corrected twice by colleagues; one real event, then mainly speech.

15.reason: R. Akiva visits Ginzak, cannot answer questions, then goes to the study hall and learns the answers; some action and change, but mainly questions and answers.

16.reason: Rav sees Rav Kahana wash his hair and rebukes him with a verse; Kahana feels cursed. One event and mainly speech, with some conflict.

17.reason: A one-line report of a wonder (wheat raining on Adi the Arab) cited to show a case is possible; nothing follows.

18.reason: A man sold his property and came before Rav Yeimar who ruled; coming before a rabbi and a ruling is not enough.

19.reason: A man dies claiming no brothers, followed by legal debate and a ruling; one event then discussion, not even borderline.

20.reason: Rav goes to a graveyard and divines the causes of death, cited as evidence of his view; some action and a discovery, but little development.
